details.theory: The rent timing is the main problem because it is a big payment at once.

diagnosis.headline: Yearly rent is tying up your kitchen cash in one big hit
diagnosis.insight: This is not just a rent problem; it is a timing problem that turns steady daily sales into one heavy bill. You already have proof the landlord can bend, because he once accepted part first and the rest later.
diagnosis.working: People still buy your jollof, fried rice, stew and swallow every day.
diagnosis.story: You told me your business is OK, and you also said the rent is yearly and comes in one big payment. You also said the landlord once took half first and the rest later, which tells me there is room to ask again before the due date.

diagnosis.meaning: What is happening is that the restaurant can keep serving, but the cash is being pulled out in a lump that the day-to-day takings cannot carry comfortably. On your own figures, the money coming in is about ₦1.4m–₦1.8m a month while running costs are about ₦1.8m a month, so your business is already running tight before rent even lands. I cannot see the cash in the till from here, so any fix has to come from what you count yourself: what is due, what is in hand, and what the landlord will accept.
diagnosis.whyItMatters: You have ₦700k in hand against ₦4.6m due, so the gap is already about ₦3.9m before anything else is paid. Your food bill alone is taking about 60%–77% of the money coming in, so if the rent stays one lump payment, every quiet week will keep squeezing the kitchen.
diagnosis.nextInvestigation: First, test whether the landlord will split the rent again before the due date. That comes first because it can ease the biggest squeeze without changing your menu, your staff, or your app sales.
steps: Call the landlord today and ask for part now, rest on an agreed date.
Write down every due payment and mark which one must move first.
Tell suppliers you are settling the overdue balance in a clear plan.

tools.title: Ask for rent split again
tools.body:
Good day [name], I want to talk about the rent due soon.
My kitchen is steady, but the full payment is heavy at once.
Can I pay part now and finish on [date]?
I will keep to the plan and follow up as agreed.
tools.when: Send today before you call or visit the landlord

tools.title: What to say to the landlord
tools.body:
Good day, [name]. I want to settle the rent, but the full amount at once is too heavy for the business.
The restaurant is trading, so I am asking for the same kind of help you gave before.
Please let me pay part now and agree the rest on [date].
tools.when: Use this on a call or face to face today

tools.title: Rent plan options
tools.body:
Option one: part now, rest on [date]
Option two: part now, part next month, rest after that
Option three: full amount on [date] if I can raise it
tools.when: Use when the landlord asks what you can do

nextStep.title: Ask for part now and a date for the rest
nextStep.why: You already said the landlord once accepted half first and the rest later, so this is the clearest test to try first.
how: Write the rent due date, what you can pay now, and the date you want for the rest.
Call or visit the landlord with a calm request for part now and a fixed follow-up date.
If they agree, write the promise down immediately and keep to it.
nextStep.measure: Whether the landlord agrees to take part now and gives a date for the rest
